title: One gas, many paths: reversible and irreversible work - expand a gas one step, eight steps and grain by grain, and see the work as an area
shortTitle: One gas, many paths: reversible and irreversible work
summary: A 2D interactive concept experience: the learner lifts weights off a piston to expand NCERT's gas (2 L at 10 atm, 25 °C) to 10 L all at once (16.0 L atm), one weight at a time (28.6 L atm) and grain by grain (32.1 L atm, approaching the reversible 32.2), seeing the work as the area under the outside-pressure path; predicts first; pushes the gas back and sees an irreversible round trip leave 64/N L atm behind; and runs NCERT Problems 5.2-5.4 (w = 0, −8.0, −32.2 L atm; ΔU = 0).
subject: Chemistry
subtopics: Work is the area under the outside-pressure path
Irreversible round trips leave work in the surroundings
Free expansion and isothermal ideal gas: ΔU = 0, q = −w
concepts: The work depends on the path; ΔU does not
The reversible path gives the most work on expansion and needs the least on compression
A reversible process can be reversed by an infinitesimal change
learningObjectives: Describe the conditions that make a process thermodynamically reversible.
Compare reversible and irreversible processes in terms of the external pressure and the equilibrium of the system with its surroundings.
Visualize pressure-volume work as the area under the p-V path for single-step, multi-step and reversible changes.
Calculate the pressure-volume work for an expansion against a constant external pressure.
Compare the work done in the same isothermal expansion carried out into vacuum, against a constant external pressure and reversibly.

verification.note: Exact fractions for every stepped path, three routes to the reversible limit, the 64/N round-trip law, NCERT Problems 5.2-5.4, the page ENGINE in Node. Flag F1: Problem 5.4 calls the gas 1 mol; it is 0.818 mol (owner-approved D1). Awaiting owner review.

interactivity: 7 scenes, each moved on by the learner
look at the gas, the weights and the water bath
lift all eight weights off at once
predict, then lift the weights one at a time (a step only at rest)
pour the sand off grain by grain (stop and resume)
the target reveal: the reversible work
predict, then push the gas back three ways and see what is left over
NCERT Problems 5.2-5.4 on the same cylinder
live p-V plot with the shaded work
lab guide: what happened, why, next
